Pi#49,!VzKT!+AWp8_zv.text: Fieldrunners style path finding by Griffpatch - How does this all work? A level made up of a grid of tiles stored in the list named '_Level'.Each tile can be 1=blank, 2=An Entrance, 3=An Exit, 4=A Wall, 5=checkered, 6=Entrance2, 7=Exit 2)Each yellow dot (enemy) on the level will start its life at an entrance and wished to find the shortest route to reach an exit.  This sounds expensive, but in fact because the level is a fixed map (at least most of the time), we can create a map that all the enemies can follow and once done leave them to their own devices to just follow it.  If the level does change, then we simply ask the 'Path Finder' sprite to rethink its map and then the enemies all follow that instead.To see how the pathfinding map is created look in the 'Path Finder' sprite.

eR=#rG{xtmhgg_oIk_X|.text: So how do we find the shortest route from any tile location on the game board to a red exit square?Figuratively, if we were to pour water on to each of the exit squares at a constant speed, then the water would spread out around all obstacles from each of these starting points and end up flooding the entire reachable board. Not only this, but if we record where the water flowed from to get to each tile first, then it is logical that to find out to the quickest exit the fastest route would be to follow the stream of water that got to that tile first.This is the process that is scripted below, working in waves that spread out by one block in all directions. One complication of this is that if two waves hit a square at the same time, then both of these directions are recorded to provide a choice of direction at runtime (while the game is being played)
